correctness.rationale: Proved for every positive room count and room size under the specified two-color strict heterophily domain. A direct counting identity bounds all challenger-vote margins when the minority fits distinct rooms, with at least four votes of strict deficit for every room containing multiple minority agents. For all-mixed three-person rooms the utility-two count forces the challenger margin to be at most the negative number of pure rooms. Boundary cases and symmetry factors in the count are checked. Standard-library exact matching and direct labeled enumerations agree in stated finite ranges; those experiments are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The problem asks for majority-undominated group partitions rather than routine welfare maximization. The characterization gives a complete natural infinite family at room size three plus arbitrary-size sparse-minority extension, a linear-time recognition/construction rule and exact counts of all outcomes. It fills a meaningful tractability/existence gap relative to known two-person popularity algorithms and variable-size hardness; no generic downstream consequence is required.
